sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: It's my last day at work tomorrow.
sentences.translationZh: 这是我明天工作的最后一天.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: I start my new job in two weeks.
sentences.translationZh: 我两周后开始新的工作.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
sentences.translationZh: 我的人力资源经理想在我离开前采访我.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Ah, an exit interview.
sentences.translationZh: 啊,一个退出采访.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Are you looking forward to it?
sentences.translationZh: 你期待吗?

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: I'm not sure how I feel about it.
sentences.translationZh: 我不知道我对它有什么感觉.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
sentences.translationZh: 我辞职是因为我对那家公司很不高兴,但我不确定我是否应该告诉他们我的感受.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview.
sentences.translationZh: 根据我的思维方式,在一次离职采访中释放出一股激起的真相,有两个主要的潜在好处.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: The first is release.
sentences.translationZh: 第一个是释放.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Unburdening yourself of frustration and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
sentences.translationZh: 让自己承受挫折 甚至愤怒的人 谁不是朋友或亲密同事 都能够解脱.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: And let me guess.
sentences.translationZh: 让我猜猜.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: The second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
sentences.translationZh: 第二,批评在理论上会帮助我离开后要改进的组织,确保未来的员工不太可能遇到我的所作所为?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: That's right.
sentences.translationZh: 没错.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen.
sentences.translationZh: 但公司改进部分的问题在于它经常不会发生.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't.
sentences.translationZh: 退出采访应该是私下的,但往往不是.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential, and the information is used as dirt against another manager or can be traded among senior managers.
sentences.translationZh: 在我的公司里,从这些访谈中获取的信息往往不保密,这些信息被用作对另一名经理的污垢,或者可以在高级管理人员之间交易.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview.
sentences.translationZh: 现在你让我在采访中 重新思考我会透露什么.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: There is always the chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.
sentences.translationZh: 总是有可能会影响我的名声和我在业界的网络能力.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: It is a pretty small industry after all.
sentences.translationZh: 毕竟这是一个相当小的行业.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Anything you initially gain from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
sentences.translationZh: 任何你最初从即时的满足中 得到的, 说它是什么, 你可能会失去 下赛道 伤害你的未来职业前景.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Right.
sentences.translationZh: 正确的。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Perhaps I would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites.
sentences.translationZh: 也许 我最好把事情从我的胸膛里拿开 去那些高薪的员工网站.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: You could, and don't do the interview at all.
sentences.translationZh: 你可以,而且不要做采访.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Exit interviews are not mandatory.
sentences.translationZh: 离职面谈不是强制性的.

Her latest documentary

Her unsuccessful journey

options.text: She was caught in a hurricane

She suffered from water shortage
She had to endure many hardships

They had no more food in the canoe
A flood was approaching
A hurricane was coming

questions.prompt: 根据录音选择最符合的一项

options.text: It was memorable
It was unbearable. '
It was fruitful
It was uneventful

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Forster.
sentences.translationZh: 今天,我和著名植物学家简·福斯特谈话.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
sentences.translationZh: 谢谢你邀请我参加节目 亨利.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity, since the release of your latest documentary.
sentences.translationZh: 最近,简,你变得相当出名 自从你最新的纪录片发布.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Can you tell us a little about it?
sentences.translationZh: 你能告诉我们一点吗?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia.
sentences.translationZh: 研究东南亚赤道地区 热带雨林的原生植被.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
sentences.translationZh: 你当然可以去一些非常异地的地方.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: It was far from glamorous, to be honest.
sentences.translationZh: 老实说,这远远没有魅力.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: The area we visited was accessible only by canoe, and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least.
sentences.translationZh: 我们访问的地区只有独木舟可以进入,而小屋的生活条件至少可以说是原始的.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: There was no electricity, and our water supply was a nearby stream.
sentences.translationZh: 没有电,我们的供水是附近的一条溪流.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
sentences.translationZh: 你在场时天气怎么样?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable.
sentences.translationZh: 天气对我们的工作毫无帮助,因为湿度几乎无法忍受.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing.
sentences.translationZh: 午后住茅屋而无所取.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: It was too humid to either work or sleep.
sentences.translationZh: 工作或睡觉都太潮湿了.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
sentences.translationZh: 你的队伍在丛林呆了多久?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Originally, we planned to be there for a month, but in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
sentences.translationZh: 最初,我们计划在那里呆一个月,但最后我们只呆了两周.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Why did you cut the expedition short?
sentences.translationZh: 你为什么缩短远征?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching, and we had to evacuate at very short notice.
sentences.translationZh: 途经中途,我们接到了飓风逼近的消息,不得不在很短时间内撤离.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
sentences.translationZh: 这听起来像一个迷人的传闻.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: It was frightening.
sentences.translationZh: 这是可怕的.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids.
sentences.translationZh: 最快的疏散路线是通过河流快车.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
sentences.translationZh: 我们不得不导航他们 携带我们的所有设备.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
sentences.translationZh: 总的来说,这次旅程没有成功吗?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Absolutely not.
sentences.translationZh: 绝对不行.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
sentences.translationZh: 我们收集了大量关于当地植物生物的数据.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
sentences.translationZh: 你为什么忍受这种不利条件?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Botany is an obsession for me.
sentences.translationZh: 植物学对我来说是一种痴迷.

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery, and I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
sentences.translationZh: 我参观过的许多目的地景色令人惊叹,我有机会与来自世界各地的各种人见面.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: So where will your next destination be?
sentences.translationZh: 那么下一个目的地在哪里?

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: I haven't decided yet.
sentences.translationZh: 我还没决定。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Then we can leave it for another occasion.
sentences.translationZh: 然后我们可以把它留给另一个场合.

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Thanks.
sentences.translationZh: 谢谢。

options.text: It ensures the accuracy of their arguments
It diminishes laymen's interest in science
It hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem
It makes their expressions more explicit

questions.prompt: 根据录音选择最符合的一项

options.text: They will see the complexity of science
They feel great respect towards scientists

questions.prompt: 根据录音选择最符合的一项

options.text: Explain all the jargon terms
Do away with jargon terms
Find appropriate topics
Stimulate their interest

sentences.text: Scientists often use specialised jargon terms while communicating with laymen.
sentences.translationZh: 科学家经常在与外行人沟通时使用专门的术语.

sentences.text: Most of them don't realise the harmful effects of this practice.
sentences.translationZh: 他们大多没有意识到这种做法的有害影响.

sentences.text: In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics but without the use of specialised terms.
sentences.translationZh: 在一项新的研究中,人们在阅读自主载体和外科机器人等科目时接触到术语,后来表示自己对科学的兴趣不如阅读相同专题但没有使用专门术语的其他人.

sentences.text: They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics.
sentences.translationZh: 他们还觉得对科学的了解较少,讨论科学专题的资格较低.

sentences.text: It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text.
sentences.translationZh: 值得注意的是,如果在正文中定义了用词,这没有任何区别.

sentences.text: Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
sentences.translationZh: 即使定义了这些术语,读者仍然感到与阅读没有被解释的词汇的读者一样缺乏参与.

sentences.text: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers.
sentences.translationZh: 问题在于,仅仅用词的存在就向读者发出了令人沮丧的信息.

sentences.text: Hilary Shulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialised words are a signal.
sentences.translationZh: 研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼(Hilary Shulman)声称,专用词是一种信号.

sentences.text: Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
sentences.translationZh: 贾刚告诉人们,信息不是给他们的.

sentences.text: There's an even darker side to how people react to jargon.
sentences.translationZh: 对于人们如何对术语作出反应,还有更黑暗的一面.

sentences.text: In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science.
sentences.translationZh: 在另一项研究中,研究人员发现,读取包含术语的科学文章使人们对实际科学产生怀疑.

sentences.text: They found the opposite when a text is easier to read.
sentences.translationZh: 当一个文本更容易被读取时,他们发现恰恰相反.

sentences.text: Then, people are more persuaded.
sentences.translationZh: 那么,人们会更信服.

sentences.text: Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects.
sentences.translationZh: 因此,在谈论复杂的科学课题时,必须明确沟通.

sentences.text: This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines.
sentences.translationZh: 公共卫生方面的问题尤其如此,如新药的安全和疫苗的好处.

sentences.text: Shulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences.
sentences.translationZh: 舒尔曼承认,对科学受众来说,使用术语是合适的.

sentences.text: But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language.
sentences.translationZh: 但是想与大众沟通的科学家需要修改自己的语言.

sentences.text: They need to eliminate jargon.
sentences.translationZh: 他们需要去除术语.

sentences.text: At the beginning of the 20th century, on the Gulf Coast in the U.S. state of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
sentences.translationZh: 20世纪初,在美国德克萨斯州的海湾海岸上,有一座山上气体渗出非常出名,有时学生会放火烧山.

sentences.text: Patio Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill.
sentences.translationZh: 巴提奥·希金斯(Patio Higgins)是一位不尽人意的当地商人,他开始相信有石油在气山下.

sentences.text: Oil wells weren't drilled back then.
sentences.translationZh: 当时没有钻油井.

sentences.text: They were essentially dug.
sentences.translationZh: 他们基本上被挖出.

sentences.text: The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole.
sentences.translationZh: 山下沙地击败了希金斯工人多次试图打出一个正宗的洞.

sentences.text: Higgins had forecast oil at 1,000 feet, a totally made-up figure.
sentences.translationZh: 希金斯预测石油在1000英尺, 一个完全编造的数字.

sentences.text: Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas.
sentences.translationZh: 希金斯随后聘请了采矿工程师安东尼·卢卡斯上尉.

sentences.text: After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
sentences.translationZh: 遇到多起挫折后,卢卡斯船长决定使用钻井,他的创新创造了现代石油钻井工业.

sentences.text: In January 1901, at 1,020 feet, almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess, the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present.
sentences.translationZh: 1901年1月,在1,020英尺处,几乎恰好是希金斯狂猜所预测的深度,井口咆哮并突然喷出泥浆和从地上喷出6吨的钻管,使在场的人感到恐惧.

sentences.text: For the next nine days until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
sentences.translationZh: 在接下来的九天里,直到井被封顶,井里倒出出比美国所有井加起来更多的石油.

sentences.text: In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry.
sentences.translationZh: 当时德克萨斯州几乎完全是农村,没有大城市,几乎没有工业.

sentences.text: Cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy.
sentences.translationZh: 棉花和牛肉是经济的基础.

sentences.text: Higgins' well changed that.
sentences.translationZh: 希金斯的好改变.

sentences.text: The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas.
sentences.translationZh: 繁荣使一些探矿者成为百万富翁,但石油突然过剩并不完全是德克萨斯的福分.

sentences.text: In the 1930s, prices crashed to the point that, in some parts of the country, oil was cheaper than water.
sentences.translationZh: 1930年代,价格暴跌,以至于在该国一些地区,石油比水便宜.

sentences.text: That would become a familiar pattern of the boom-or-bust Texas economy.
sentences.translationZh: 这将成为德克萨斯州经济繁荣或萧条的常见模式.

questions.prompt: 根据录音选择最符合的一项

options.text: It was based only on the perspective of employees
It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem
It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view
It collected feedback from both employers and employees

sentences.text: Most people dislike their jobs.
sentences.translationZh: 大多数人不喜欢他们的工作.

sentences.text: It's an astonishing but statistical fact.
sentences.translationZh: 这是一个惊人但统计事实.

sentences.text: A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.
sentences.translationZh: 据新研究,雇员不满的一个主要原因是许多人认为他们有可怕的管理人员.

sentences.text: Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative, though.
sentences.translationZh: 不过,很少有人说他们的管理人员是恶意的或操纵性的.

sentences.text: While those types certainly exist, they're a minority.
sentences.translationZh: 虽然这些类型确实存在,但他们是少数.

sentences.text: The majority of managers seemingly just don't know any better.
sentences.translationZh: 大部分的经理似乎都不太清楚.

sentences.text: They're often emulating bad managers they've had in the past.
sentences.translationZh: 他们经常模仿过去有过的坏管理者.

sentences.text: It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course.
sentences.translationZh: 很可能他们从未读过管理书籍或上过管理课程.

sentences.text: They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
sentences.translationZh: 他们甚至可能没有反思良好的管理是什么样子,以及如何影响自己的管理风格.

sentences.text: The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had.
sentences.translationZh: 研究人员采访了员工关于他们的经理,首先问到他们曾经有过的最差的经理.

sentences.text: From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
sentences.translationZh: 从中,研究人员想出四个主要原因,为什么一些管理人员被认为在工作上太糟糕了.

sentences.text: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices.
sentences.translationZh: 第一个原因是公司文化,雇员认为公司文化助长了不良的管理做法.

sentences.text: It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training, and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy.
sentences.translationZh: 特别值得责备的是紧张的工作环境、很少的培训以及缺乏问责制.

sentences.text: Often, a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings.
sentences.translationZh: 通常,经理的上司在未能惩戒个人的错失行为时,可以有效地鼓励经理的厌恶行为.

sentences.text: Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
sentences.translationZh: 这种工作场所有时被描述为有毒.

sentences.text: The second cause was attributed to the manager's characteristics.
sentences.translationZh: 第二个原因是管理人员的特征.

sentences.text: Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people, those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
sentences.translationZh: 被认为最具破坏性的人是奇特的人、没有开车的人、允许个人问题进入工作场所的人,以及脾气或性格普遍不愉快的人.

sentences.text: The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications.
sentences.translationZh: 管理不善的第三个原因是资格不足.

sentences.text: Not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
sentences.translationZh: 并不是从大学获得的正式种类,而是从可信的工作经验和专业成就中获得的非正式种类.

sentences.text: The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential.
sentences.translationZh: 第四个原因涉及因潜力之外的原因被提升的管理人员.

sentences.text: One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest.
sentences.translationZh: 这些人之所以被提拔的原因之一是,他们的时间最长.

sentences.text: It wasn't their skill set or other merits that got them the job.
sentences.translationZh: 不是他们的技能或其他优点 让他们得到这份工作.

sentences.text: It was their tenure.
sentences.translationZh: 这是他们的任期.

sentences.text: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees.
sentences.translationZh: 值得指出的一点是,这项研究只是从雇员的角度出发的.

sentences.text: The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers.
sentences.translationZh: 研究者没有问高层领导人对前线管理人员的看法.

sentences.text: It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.
sentences.translationZh: 他们很可能会满足于他们所提升的个人 是如何表现的, 他们对他们所实际造成的破坏非常的无知, 这或许可以解释为什么,正如研究者所得出的结论, 同样的中层管理者 通常不知道他们是一个糟糕的管理者.

sentences.text: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
sentences.translationZh: 随着无驾驶车辆的使用似乎不可避免,澳大利亚广阔的西澳大利亚沙漠州的矿业公司无疑正在带头.

sentences.text: Iron ore is a key ingredient in steelmaking.
sentences.translationZh: 铁矿石是炼钢的关键成分.

sentences.text: The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year.
sentences.translationZh: 这里的矿业公司每年出产铁矿石近3亿吨.

sentences.text: The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use in the Western Australian mines can weigh 400 tons fully loaded and travel at speeds of up to 60 km per hour.
sentences.translationZh: 西澳大利亚州矿区正在使用的240辆大型自发卡车可重400吨,可满载,行驶速度可达每小时60公里.

sentences.text: They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations.
sentences.translationZh: 它们是一个技术飞跃,沿着从矿山到目的地数百公里的路线运输铁矿石.

sentences.text: Here, when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operations center direct it precisely where to unload.
sentences.translationZh: 在这里,当卡车到达目的地时,行动中心的工作人员指示它确切的卸货地点.

sentences.text: Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
sentences.translationZh: 大量铁矿石再由自主列车运送到海港.

sentences.text: Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever.
sentences.translationZh: 辩护人认为这些自动车辆会永远地改变采矿.

sentences.text: It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
sentences.translationZh: 使用自动化技术可能只有5年时间才能导致一个完全的机器人矿.

sentences.text: A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution.
sentences.translationZh: 一系列因素将西澳大利亚的沙漠地区推向了这次自动化革命的先行.

sentences.text: These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment, and the repetitive nature of some of the work.
sentences.translationZh: 其中包括地雷的巨大规模、设备的规模以及一些工作的重复性.

sentences.text: Then there's the area's remoteness.
sentences.translationZh: 后为地处偏僻地.

sentences.text: At 502,000 square kilometers, it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge.
sentences.translationZh: 在502,000平方千米的地方,它有时会使招聘工作人员成为一项挑战.

sentences.text: Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery.
sentences.translationZh: 另一个考虑因素是人类与大型机械相互作用的风险.

sentences.text: There are also the financial imperatives.
sentences.translationZh: 还有财政上的必要.

sentences.text: The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
sentences.translationZh: 矿业公司不断推动提高生产率和效率,这是采用自动化技术的另一个强大动力.

sentences.text: The concept of a fully autonomous mine is a bit of a misleading term, however.
sentences.translationZh: 然而,一个完全自治的地雷的概念有点误导人.

sentences.text: This is because the more technology is put into the field, the more people are needed to deploy, maintain, and improve it.
sentences.translationZh: 这是因为技术投入实地越多,就越需要部署、维护和改进.

sentences.text: The automation and digitization of the industry is creating a need for different jobs.
sentences.translationZh: 该行业的自动化和数字化正在产生对不同工作的需求.

sentences.text: These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence.
sentences.translationZh: 其中包括自动化和人工智能方面的数据科学家和工程师.

sentences.text: The mining companies claim automation and robotics present opportunities to make mining more sustainable and safer.
sentences.translationZh: 采矿公司声称,自动化和机器人技术提供了使采矿更具可持续性和更安全的机会.

sentences.text: Employees will be offered a career that is even more fulfilling and more rewarding.
sentences.translationZh: 雇员将获得一个更加充实和更有回报的职业.

sentences.text: Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology, but they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology.
sentences.translationZh: 工人工会已经接受了引进新技术的必然性,但对自动化技术的兴起仍有保留.

sentences.text: Their main concern is the potential impact on remote communities.
sentences.translationZh: 他们的主要关切是对偏远社区的潜在影响.

sentences.text: As automation spreads further, the question is how these remote communities will survive when the old jobs are eliminated.
sentences.translationZh: 随着自动化进一步普及,问题是这些偏远社区在被淘汰了的旧工作后如何活下来.

sentences.text: And this may well prove to be the most significant impact of robotic technology in many places around the world.
sentences.translationZh: 这很可能是机器人技术 在世界许多地方最显著的影响.

sentences.text: According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road death rate is almost double the global average.
sentences.translationZh: 据官方统计,泰国的年度公路死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍.

sentences.text: Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
sentences.translationZh: 泰国人知道他们的道路很危险,但他们不知道这很容易被改变.

sentences.text: Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease.
sentences.translationZh: 在全球范围内,每年交通事故造成的死亡人数比任何传染病都要多.

sentences.text: Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America put the death toll in 2017 at 1.24 million.
sentences.translationZh: 美国健康计量与评价研究所的研究人员在2017年的死亡人数为124万.

sentences.text: According to the Institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century.
sentences.translationZh: 根据该研究所,自世纪之交以来,死亡总人数几乎是静止不变的.

sentences.text: But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
sentences.translationZh: 但这掩盖了个别国家的许多变化.

sentences.text: In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before.
sentences.translationZh: 在许多穷国,道路事故造成的死亡人数比以往任何时候都多.

sentences.text: Those countries have swelling, young populations, a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes, and a limited supply of surgeons.
sentences.translationZh: 这些国家人口膨胀,年轻,汽车和摩托车车队迅速增长,外科医生供应有限.

sentences.text: It is impossible to know for sure because official statistics are so inadequate.
sentences.translationZh: 由于官方统计如此不足,不可能确定.

sentences.text: But deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low-income countries.
sentences.translationZh: 但许多低收入国家的死亡率被认为自1990年以来已上升了40%.

sentences.text: In many rich countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer.
sentences.translationZh: 相形之下,在许多富国,道路变得更加安全.

sentences.text: In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of deaths has fallen by about two-thirds since the late 1990s.
sentences.translationZh: 例如,在爱沙尼亚和爱尔兰,自1990年代后期以来,死亡人数已下降了大约三分之二.

sentences.text: But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle-income countries, which contain most of the world's people and most dangerous roads.
sentences.translationZh: 但最重要的和令人感兴趣的变化发生在中等收入国家,这些国家包括世界上大多数人口和最危险的道路.

sentences.text: According to researchers, in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000 and in India since 2012.
sentences.translationZh: 研究者认为,在中国和南非,自2000年以来,交通死亡人数一直在下降,自2012年以来,印度的交通死亡人数也在下降.

sentences.text: And the Philippines reached its peak four years ago.
sentences.translationZh: 而菲律宾在四年前达到顶峰.

sentences.text: The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
sentences.translationZh: 问题是泰国是否能够很快效仿.

sentences.text: Rob McKinney, head of the International Road Assessment Program, says that all countries tend to go through three phases.
sentences.translationZh: 国际道路评估方案负责人罗布·麦金尼(Rob McKinney)表示,所有国家都倾向于经历三个阶段.

sentences.text: They begin with poor, slow roads.
sentences.translationZh: 他们从贫穷而缓慢的道路开始.

sentences.text: In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate.
sentences.translationZh: 在第二阶段,随着他们日益富裕,他们铺平了道路,使交通能够更快地前进并推进了死亡率.

sentences.text: Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer.
sentences.translationZh: 最后,在第三阶段,各国采取行动使道路更加安全.

sentences.text: The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
sentences.translationZh: 因此,技巧是通过更早和更密切地关注致命事故,更快地达到第三阶段.

sentences.text: How to do that?
sentences.translationZh: 怎么样?

sentences.text: The solution lies not just in better infrastructure but in better social incentives.
sentences.translationZh: 解决办法不仅在于改善基础设施,而且在于更好的社会鼓励措施.

sentences.text: Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't.
sentences.translationZh: 安全驾驶习惯是人们知道应该遵循的习惯,但往往不遵循.

sentences.text: Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait, as some imagine.
sentences.translationZh: 危险驾车并不是某些人想象的固定的文化特征.

sentences.text: People respond to incentives such as traffic laws that are actually enforced.
sentences.translationZh: 人们会回应实际执行的交通法等激励措施.
